role.altitude: The rolling mill operator keeps choosing tooling, judging wear, taking mills apart and handling heavy parts; looking up roll sets in paper charts, searching racks and writing tooling logs shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the tooling register and barcode labels
role.ambitious_version: An operator who knows where every roll set is and how worn it is before walking to the rack.

tasks.short: Look up rolls, dies, roll stands and chucks in data charts, select them to form specified contours, and collect them from storage.

steps.what: Operator looks up rolls, dies, roll stands and chucks in the data charts for the product
Operator selects the tooling to form the specified contours, allowing for wear and available sets
Operator finds the selected rolls and dies in the storage racks
Operator carries the rolls and dies to the mill

tasks.design: A tooling table in the production system shows, per product, the roll set, dies, stand configuration and chucks, with each set's wear status and rack location, instead of paper data charts. Choosing the tooling stays with the operator. The rack location cuts the search; carrying and handling the tooling keep their full time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data charts were on paper and locations were in people's heads.
tasks.still_hard: Special products with no standard tooling.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a roll's surface will mark the product.
tasks.altitude: Less looking up and searching; choosing stays.

reach.learn: Whether worn sets are flagged earlier.

evidence.claim: Production systems record data per workplace and machine.
Tooling registers with locations and wear status are standard records apps.

assumptions: Boundary: selecting tooling; reading rolling orders (task 10094) and calculating draft and roll speed (task 10105) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: product to tooling mapping entered once from the data charts by the tool room.
unknowns: Number of roll sets in use.

incremental.description: Operator updates set locations when returning tooling.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few products with simple tooling; high: many products and roll sets.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Disassemble sizing mills removed from rolling lines, inspect parts for wear, sort and store parts, and record what was stored.

steps.what: Operator disassembles sizing mills removed from the rolling line
Operator inspects the parts for wear and damage
Operator sorts and stores the parts
Operator records stored and worn parts in the tooling log

tasks.design: Disassembling, inspecting, sorting and storing stay hands-on and keep their time. Racks have fixed barcoded locations per part type, and the operator scans part and location with a wear note from a pick list into the tooling register instead of writing in a paper log; only that record step is priced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Storage and wear were recorded in a paper log.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling a bearing that is about to fail.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; the work is physical.

reach.learn: Whether worn parts are known before the next changeover.

evidence.claim: Barcode records apps replace paper logs for stored parts.

assumptions: Boundary: disassembling and storing; directing roll changes (task 10100) is a sibling task.
Disassembling and inspecting keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of sizing mills changed per week.
research_questions: Are parts found faster at the next changeover?

incremental.description: Operator relabels parts with worn barcodes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few changeovers; high: frequent changeovers with many parts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

job.title: Rolling Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
